title: The Morning Breaks, I Place My Hand in Thine
description: The Morning Breaks, I Place My Hand in Thine in Tonic Solfa to SONG TWENTY-TWO, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900), headed “A Morning Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Tens (10.10.10.10), and this page sets them to SONG TWENTY-TWO; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: The morn-ing breaks, I place my hand in Thine, My God, 'tis Thine to lead, to fol-low mine; No word de-ceit-ful shall I speak the while, Nor shall I stain my hand with ac-tion vile.

lines: The morning breaks, I place my hand in Thine,
My God, 'tis Thine to lead, to follow mine;
No word deceitful shall I speak the while,
Nor shall I stain my hand with action vile.
Thine be the day with worthy labour filled,
Strong would I stand to do the duty willed;
Nor swayed by restless passion let me be,
That I may give the offering pure to Thee;
Else were I 'shamed when hoary age I see,
Shamed were this board that bears Thy gifts to me:
Mine is the impulse; O my Christ, I pray,
Be Thou Thyself to me the Blessed Way!

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to SONG TWENTY-TWO by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
